title: The Save Stone
tagline: a game that survives being closed
hints: `#include <fstream>`. Writing: `std::ofstream out("save.txt");` then `out << ...` exactly like std::cout.
Reading: `std::ifstream in("save.txt");` then `in >> hp >> maxHp;` exactly like std::cin.
`if (!in)` is how you ask whether the file opened. A missing file is not a crash - it is a stream that reports failure, and you must check.

Mixing `>>` and `getline` on a file has the SAME leftover-newline problem as std::cin. After reading the item count with `>>`, call `in.ignore(10000, '
');` before your getline loop.
The streams close themselves when they go out of scope. That is RAII, and floor 20 is about why it matters.
